candidate_relations.reason: Sinusoidal nests of mitotically active spindle cells with erythrocyte-filled spaces, vascular invasion, and irregular reticulin match hemangiosarcoma.
Neoplasm is true of an invasive mitotic tumor but does not specify vascular (hemangiosarcoma) differentiation.
Hyperplasia cannot account for vascular invasion, frequent mitoses, and an irregular reticulin network within tumor aggregates.
Focal nodular hyperplasia is a benign hepatocellular nodular lesion, not sinusoidal sarcoma with local vascular invasion.
Liver-cell adenoma is a hepatocellular neoplasm, whereas the cells form unencapsulated sinusoidal sheets with erythrocyte-filled clefts.
Liver disease is a vague parent and omits the histologic hemangiosarcoma.
Hepatocellular carcinoma would show hepatoid trabeculae, not spindle-to-polygonal cells lining dilated sinusoids with reticulin wrapping tumor nests.
Hepatic angiosarcoma is the same vascular malignancy arising in the left lateral lobe sinusoids of this rat.
Hepatic adenoma is encapsulated and hepatocellular; this lesion is unencapsulated, mitotic, and locally invasive into vessels.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: hepatic adenoma vs invasive vascular tumor

candidate_relations.reason: Hepatoblastoma is an epithelial embryonal tumor, not a reticulin-rich sinusoidal vascular sarcoma.
Embryonal sarcoma of the liver lacks the erythrocyte-filled intercellular spaces and sinusoidal endothelial pattern recorded here.
Hepatic neoplasia is the organ-level parent and does not specify hemangiosarcoma.
Cholangiocarcinoma is a glandular biliary tumor, not spindle cells in dilated sinusoids with vascular invasion.
Bile-duct carcinoma likewise names an epithelial biliary malignancy rather than the reticulin-wrapped vascular tumor.
Liver hemangioma is a benign vascular lesion and conflicts with hyperchromasia, frequent mitoses, necrosis, and vessel invasion.
